source: Galaxy clusters: Abell, Corwin & Olowin 1989, ApJS 70, 1 (VizieR VII/110A), redshifts from Struble & Rood 1987. Quasars: Véron-Cetty & Véron 2010, A&A 518, A10, 13th edition (VizieR VII/258), V < 17.5 or z ≥ 5. Record holders from the papers cited with each. Positions in galactic coordinates; distances from redshift (flat ΛCDM, H0 = 70, Ωm = 0.3).

records.name: JADES-GS-z14-0
records.note: The most distant galaxy confirmed by spectroscopy (as of 2024), seen 290 million years after the Big Bang.

records.name: GN-z11
records.note: A luminous galaxy 430 million years after the Big Bang, the most distant known before JWST.

records.name: J0313−1806
records.note: The most distant quasar known, with a 1.6-billion-solar-mass black hole 670 million years after the Big Bang.

records.name: ULAS J1120+0641
records.note: The first quasar found beyond redshift 7.

records.name: TON 618
records.note: A hyperluminous quasar whose black hole may weigh 40 billion suns, one of the heaviest known.

records.name: 3C 273
records.note: The first quasar identified (1963) and the brightest in our sky: its light left two billion years ago, yet an amateur telescope shows it.
